How to Change the Oil in Your Rig

to add to this:

don't overtighten your drain plug; most oil pans are aluminum and you can atirp it out easily with the steel bolt. As long as it's not dripping when you're all done, it's tight enough. Check fot drips under your car after 50-100 miles and tighten a little if needed.

copper washers are the best for sealing your drain plug

be wary of using a pair of oil filter pliers; you may need then to take off an overtightened filter but your new filter only needs to go on hand-tight. Don't squeeze to hard with the pliers or you can rip up a shitty, overtight filter - good luck if that happens. PS never try stabbing a screwdriver through the filter in lieu of a wrench/pliers to try to remove it

The article mentions that you can get this done for less than $20; bull-fucking-shit. If you're spending less than $20 on your oil and filter, you're either changing the oil on a lawnmower of you're a cheapskate idiot. Buy decent oil - your selection will depend greatly on what your weight of oil your engine requires and how much it takes. For instance, my car takes 5qts of 0W-20, that oil costs about $25 to $35 for 5qts depending on the brand and how many marketing buzzwords are slapped on the bottle. I keep an extra quart in my trunk just in case. Total oil change will cost me at least $30 each time.

while your engine oil is draining into your cath pan, take a few minutes to wipe up the grime on your engine, check your belts, and check your engine air filter. If your belts are shiny or cracked, it's time to replace it/them. If your air filter is darker than pure white, replace it.

Keep a can of brake cleaner nearby, it's the best degreaser/cleaner around. Avoid spraying anything plastic/rubber with it.
